A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, identify represented billed revenue (invoices) that are associated with counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with counterparty and contract identifiers as they appear in the sources.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
exclusions: expired statements of work are not active contracts
invoices whose invoice-to-contract association cannot be confidently established are not silently dropped

world_eligible: invoice referent with amount, currency, period, status, billed_name as sourced
contract referent with identifier as it appears in sources
contract document type and temporal status (e.g. active vs expired)

parsed contractual clause text and clause kind (change-of-control consent/notice, change-of-control termination, assignment consent/notice/restriction including affiliate-only or competitor prohibition)
purpose_bound: acquisition-relevant condition: purpose-defined subset of clause kinds that trigger inclusion
qualifying invoice: invoice included in output because its associated active contract bears an acquisition-relevant condition
association asserted: confident join between billed name and contract counterparty
association unresolved: billed name and contract counterparty cannot be confidently joined

epistemic_requirements: Missing identity linkage is not a negative contractual finding.
If a billed name and a contract counterparty cannot be confidently associated, record association as unresolved rather than omitting the invoice or asserting the join.
Positive association requires establishing evidence; compatibility or name similarity alone is insufficient.
Report identifiers exactly as they appear in authoritative sources (no silent canonicalization in the purpose output).

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: invoice is reported but invoice-to-contract/counterparty linkage is not confidently established

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: every invoice that qualifies under purpose policies (active contract with acquisition-relevant condition) must appear in invoices
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: each emitted invoice row must include invoice_id, billed_name, amount, currency, period, status, contract_id, and association
completeness_expectations.identifier_fidelity: contract_id and invoice_id values must match source rendering conventions
non_goals: complete enumeration of all invoices in the data room
closed-world assertion that non-qualifying invoices lack acquisition-relevant exposure

acquisition_relevant_conditions: require consent or notice on a change of control
permit termination upon a change of control
require consent or notice before assignment, including assignment restricted except to affiliates or assignment prohibited to a competitor
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_policy: an expired statement of work is not an active contract
purpose_specific_policies.row_inclusion_rule: include an invoice when it has an asserted or unresolved association to a contract that is active under this purpose and contains at least one acquisition-relevant condition
purpose_specific_policies.world_vs_purpose_boundary: whether a clause kind is acquisition-relevant and whether a contract counts as active for this analytical question are purpose policies; parsed clause presence, contract dates, and sourced invoice facts are world-eligible propositions

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, reconcile represented customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, the company registry, and contracts; for each commercially relevant name or record, state whether it is confidently the same legal counterparty as other records or whether identification remains unresolved.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
entities_in_scope: commercially relevant names and records across the four systems
candidate legal entities in the registry tied to commercial relationships
exclusions: global merges based solely on orthographic or fuzzy name similarity
automatic collapse of distinct registry entities that share similar trade names

required_output_shape.ordering: sort links by left ascending, then right ascending

world_eligible: referents for CRM accounts, billed names, registry company numbers, and contract filenames
sourced legal names, trade names, and registry attributes as observed
mechanical normalization of exact legal-form variants of the same registered name
purpose_bound: SAME_ENTITY: confident positive judgment that two referents denote the same legal counterparty
DISTINCT: confident negative judgment that two referents denote different legal counterparties
UNRESOLVED: insufficient evidence for a positive same-entity or distinct judgment
required link set: links needed to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the governing contract, and registry rows that are candidate legal entities for that relationship

epistemic_requirements: Do not globally merge records merely because two names look similar.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical equivalences.
Distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party.
Permit explicit unresolved identity; absence of a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative judgment.
SAME_ENTITY and DISTINCT require bounded establishing evidence, not mere compatibility.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: identity relationship between left and right referents is not confidently resolved

completeness_expectations.link_coverage: include every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: each link must include left, right, and epistemic
non_goals: exhaustive all-pairs comparison of every name in the data room
closed-world completion of the identity graph beyond required commercial relationship links

purpose_specific_policies.merge_prohibition: no global merge on superficial name similarity
purpose_specific_policies.mechanical_equivalence_allowance: exact legal-form variants of the same registered name
purpose_specific_policies.required_link_topology: CRM account ↔ billed name ↔ governing contract ↔ candidate registry entity
purpose_specific_policies.world_vs_purpose_boundary: sourced names and registry rows are world observations; which pairs must be linked for commercial diligence and the threshold for SAME_ENTITY vs DISTINCT vs UNRESOLVED are purpose policies

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under a two-part test combining current commercial relationship and specific contractual obligation kinds.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
entities_in_scope: counterparties identified with Purpose B identifier forms
open invoices tied to commercial relationships
exclusions: expired contracts do not create current dependency
one-off paid historical invoices without an active contract do not create current dependency

required_output_shape.identifier_forms: same as Purpose B (crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:)
required_output_shape.ordering: sort dependencies by contract_id ascending; obligation_kinds sorted within each row

world_eligible: parsed clause kinds: exclusivity, auto-renewal, rolling term with notice-to-terminate mechanics
referential links between invoices, contracts, and counterparties when confidently established
purpose_bound: current commercial relationship: open invoice OR active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term
commercially dependent: both current relationship and at least one listed obligation kind in an active contract
status dependent: both prongs satisfied under purpose rules with resolvable identity
status unresolved: dependency cannot be affirmed because required identity joins are unresolved

epistemic_requirements: If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report status as unresolved rather than dependent or as a false negative.
Do not infer non-dependency from missing or incomplete identity reconciliation.
Dependency is a purpose analytical construct; underlying invoice, contract, and clause facts remain world-eligible.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: commercial dependency cannot be established because identity or join evidence required by the two-part test is unresolved

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: emit a dependency row for each counterparty-contract pair that meets purpose inclusion criteria or must be reported as unresolved under the identity rule
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: each row includes counterparty, contract_id, open_invoice_ids, obligation_kinds, and status
non_goals: enumeration of all counterparties with no current relationship
closed-world negation that non-listed pairs are independent

dependency_test.prong_1_current_relationship: open invoice OR active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term
dependency_test.prong_2_obligation: active contract contains exclusivity, term auto-renewal, or rolling term continuing unless notice is given

purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_for_dependency: expired contracts excluded; rolling/auto-renew continuation counts as active
purpose_specific_policies.historical_invoice_exclusion: one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not satisfy prong 1
purpose_specific_policies.identity_dependency: relies on Purpose B identifier forms and identity judgments; unresolved identity forces status unresolved
purpose_specific_policies.world_vs_purpose_boundary: sourced invoice status, contract term structure, and parsed clause kinds are world-eligible; the composite dependent/unresolved classification and the current-relationship threshold are purpose policies
